Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

feed verb

give food to

also feeding

classical

Cic. Off. 2.14: bēstiās pāscere (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 6.1.13: holusculīs nōs solēs pāscere
Traupman 166, 314

pāscō, pāscere, pāvī, pāstum

verb, third conjugation

feed (an animal, a person)

First of animals, which it also takes out to graze; of people too, as when Cicero teases Atticus for always feeding him vegetables. The passive pāscor is to feed, to graze.

Other words

  • cibō, cibāre, —, cibātum — give food to (animals)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Suet. Tib. 72 (Lewis & Short); Col. 8.11.15 (Lewis & Short)

    Rare. Suetonius’s Tiberius fed his pet snake by hand; with people as object the verb is late (Vulgate).

  • alō, alere, aluī, altum — nourish, feed and bring up

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Tac. Germ. 20.1: sua quemque māter ūberibus alit

    Feeding that brings up: a mother nursing her baby.

Examples

  • vēlōcēs Spartae catulōs ācremque Molossum pāsce serō pinguī

    feed the swift Spartan puppies and the fierce mastiff on rich wheyVerg. G. 3.405–406

  • Respicite volātilia caelī … et Pater vester caelestis pāscit illa.

    Look at the birds of the air … and your heavenly Father feeds them.Vulg. Mt. 6.26

See also eat, be hungry.
